def experiments_for_many(
    self, accessions: Iterable[str], *, partial: bool = False
) -> dict[str, list[Experiment]] | Partial[dict[str, list[Experiment]]]:
    """Map each accession to the SRA experiments under it, built from stored packages.

    Walks down one level at a time, with one link lookup and one holdings lookup per
    level for all roots together.

    Parameters
    ----------
    accessions : iterable of str
        The roots of the walk.
    partial : bool
        Return what is held instead of raising ``NotMirrored``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict or Partial
        Each root mapped to its sorted experiments. With ``partial=True``, a ``Partial``
        whose ``held`` is that mapping over held records and whose ``missing`` lists every
        accession the walk reached but the store does not hold.

    Raises
    ------
    AccessionError
        If an accession is malformed.
    NotFound
        If no snapshot lists a root, even with ``partial``.
    NotMirrored
        If a root or a record on the way down is not held, unless ``partial``. The
        message lists every missing accession.
    """
    roots = _accessions(accessions)
    missing = self._require_held(set(roots), not_held_ok=True)
    found: dict[str, set[str]] = {r: set() for r in roots}
    level = {(r, r) for r in roots if r not in missing}
    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    while level:
        seen |= level
        todo = set()
        for root, acc in level:
            if kind_of(acc) == "SRA experiment":
                found[root].add(acc)
            else:
                todo.add((root, acc))
        if not todo:
            break
        children: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
        for row in self.backend.links_many({acc for _, acc in todo}):
            for end, link in _ends(row):
                if _leads_down(kind_of(end), link):
                    children.setdefault(end, set()).add(link.other)
        reached = {c for cs in children.values() for c in cs}
        held = self.backend.held_many(reached) if reached else set()
        missing |= reached - held
        level = {
            (root, child)
            for root, acc in todo
            for child in children.get(acc, ())
            if child in held
        } - seen
    if missing and not partial:
        raise NotMirrored(f"not held in this store: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
    wanted = {acc for accs in found.values() for acc in accs}
    packages = self.backend.raw_many(wanted) if wanted else {}
    built = {
        experiment.accession: experiment
        for experiment in experiments_from_package_xml(
            "".join(text for text, _ in packages.values()),
            client=OfflineEntrezClient(),
            sdl_client=OfflineSdlClient(),
        )
    }
    result = {r: [built[a] for a in sorted(found[r]) if a in built] for r in roots}
    return Partial(result, tuple(sorted(missing))) if partial else result

def experiments_for(
    self, accession: str, *, partial: bool = False
) -> list[Experiment] | Partial[list[Experiment]]:
    """Return the SRA experiments under one accession, sorted, with no network call.

    The store twin of :func:`labdata.experiments_for`: the same ``Experiment`` type,
    built from the stored package XML by the same parser. Their properties, and their
    runs', never call NCBI; ``Run.files`` and ``Run.original_files`` raise instead.

    accessions.

        return Partial(walk.held[key], walk.missing)
    return self.experiments_for_many([accession])[key]

    The only call that imports pyarrow.

    where : str or None

        It is trusted SQL from the caller, pasted into the query as written.

        ``content_hash`` and ``snapshot_date``, then one column per field.

    ------
    ValueError

def open_store(root: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> Store:
    """Open the store, resolving its root without network or prompt.

    The root is the first of: the ``root`` argument, ``LABDATA_STORE``, then the per-user
    pointer file written by ``labdata store configure``. Opening writes nothing in the store.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : str or os.PathLike or None

        The opened store.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreNotConfiguredError
        If no root is set anywhere.
    NotAStoreError
        If the root has no ``labdata-store.toml``.
    """
    if root is None:
        root = os.environ.get(STORE_ENV, "").strip() or _from_pointer()

            "or run `labdata store configure <root>`"

    return Store(root=path, settings=read_marker(path))

    """Create the store root if missing and write its marker, ``format_version = 1``.

    The marker appears whole or not at all, and nothing else in the root is touched.

    LabdataError

    marker = path / MARKER
    tmp = temp_beside(marker, "init")

    finally:

    return marker

items.title: pipeline
items.text:
Drive one round of the full run with Snakemake: fetch, pack, extract, build, prune, copy.

The DAG lives in the packaged pipeline.smk. Each step is a labdata store subcommand, so labdata owns what a step does and Snakemake owns the order and the resume: a step's marker appears only when the step exits cleanly, and a rerun starts at the first step without one. An ncbi resource caps the network steps apart from --cores, and a mem_mb resource keeps the steps that run at once inside the job's memory.

A round's markers, logs and Snakemake state sit in <root>/work/run/<round>/, where the round names the geo-series snapshot date and the sample fraction, e.g. 2026-10-14-f0.01. Every snakemake call goes through :func:_run_snakemake, the seam tests replace.

def memory_plan(total_mb: int) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Return each step's memory in MB, so the steps that can run at once fit in ``total_mb``.

    The fetch lanes, the target list and pack run beside a snapshot extract and take a small
    share each; the extract takes the rest. The build and coverage run alone with all of it.
    """
    geo, lane = total_mb // 16, total_mb // 8
    return {
        "targets": lane,
        "geo": geo,
        "eutils": lane,
        "pack": lane,
        "extract": total_mb - geo - lane,
        "build": total_mb,
        "coverage": total_mb,
        "prune": lane,
        "copy": lane,
    }

def run(
    root: Path,
    *,
    fraction: float | None = None,
    cores: int | None = None,
    ncbi: int = NCBI_STEPS,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> int:
    """Run one round: the seeded sample of ``fraction`` of the target list, or all of it.

    The round uses the newest snapshot of every source and records their dates in
    ``run.json`` in its folder. A rerun of the same round resumes at the first unfinished
    step; the fetch steps skip every item already saved, by this round or a smaller one. A
    fetch lane that left items failed runs again, and so does every step after it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    fraction : float or None
        The round's sample of the target list, in (0, 1]; ``None`` or ``1`` for all of it.
    cores : int or None
        Cores the steps may use; defaults to :func:`labdata.store.extract.default_workers`.
    ncbi : int
        Network steps that may run at once.
    verbose : bool
        Show Snakemake's and each step's output.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Snakemake's exit code: ``0`` when every step finished, coverage included.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If a snapshot source has no snapshot.
    ValueError
        If the fraction is not in (0, 1].
    """
    fraction = targets.check_fraction(fraction)
    store = open_store(root)
    root = store.root
    dates = {source: snapshots.snapshot(root, source).date for source in extract.SOURCES}
    geo_date = dates[snapshots.GEO_SERIES]
    work = round_dir(root, geo_date, fraction)
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # --forcerun reruns a rule and every rule after it, even where their markers exist.
    rerun = []
    for lane, rule in LANES.items():
        if (work / f"{lane}.failed").is_file():
            logger.info("the %s lane left items failed last time; it runs again", lane)
            rerun.append(rule)
    cores = cores or extract.default_workers()
    memory = int(extract.allocation_mb() * STEPS_SHARE)
    labdata = f"{shlex.quote(sys.executable)} -m labdata"
    config = {
        "labdata": labdata,
        "root": str(root),
        "fraction": "" if fraction is None else repr(fraction),
        "snapshots": dates,
        "targets": str(targets.list_path(root, geo_date, fraction)),
        "copy": bool(store.settings.get(gcs.COPY_TO_KEY)),
        "mem_mb": memory_plan(memory),
    }
    config_path = work / "config.json"
    config_path.write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    started = dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    record = {"fraction": fraction, "snapshots": dates, "started": started}
    (work / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    logger.info("round %s: snapshots %s", work.name, dates)
    argv = [
        "--snakefile",
        str(_snakefile()),
        "--directory",
        str(work),
        "--cores",
        str(cores),
        "--resources",
        f"ncbi={ncbi}",
        f"mem_mb={memory}",
        "--configfile",
        str(config_path),
        "--printshellcmds",
        *RESILIENCE_FLAGS,
        *(["--forcerun", *rerun] if rerun else []),
    ]
    return _run_snakemake(argv, verbose=verbose)

The target Series list: the sequencing Series of one dated geo-series snapshot.

A Series is a target when its esummary gdstype names high-throughput sequencing, whatever its SOFT !Series_type says. The list is streamed from the snapshot into <root>/work/targets/geo-series-<date>.parquet once per snapshot date; a build or a coverage check remakes it when missing.

def in_sample(accession: str, fraction: float) -> bool:
    """Return whether a Series is in the seeded sample of ``fraction`` of the target list.

    Examples

    True

    digest = hashlib.blake2b(f"{SEED}:{accession}".encode(), digest_size=8).digest()
    return int.from_bytes(digest) < fraction * 2**64

def target_list(root: Path, date: str | None = None, fraction: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Return the target Series list of one ``geo-series`` snapshot, writing it if missing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    date : str or None
        The snapshot date; defaults to the newest snapshot.
    fraction : float or None
        A round's seeded sample of the list (see :func:`in_sample`); ``None`` or ``1`` for all.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        A Parquet file of ``accession``, ``gdstype`` and ``bioproject`` (empty when the
        snapshot gives none), one row per target Series, in snapshot order.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If the store has no such snapshot.
    ValueError
        If the fraction is not in (0, 1].
    """
    fraction = check_fraction(fraction)
    snap = snapshots.snapshot(root, snapshots.GEO_SERIES, date)
    out = list_path(root, snap.date, fraction)
    if out.is_file():
        return out
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = temp_beside(out)
    try:
        with pq.ParquetWriter(tmp, SCHEMA) as writer:
            batch: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
            for row in _targets(snap.path):
                if fraction is not None and not in_sample(row[0], fraction):
                    continue
                batch.append(row)
                if len(batch) == _BATCH:
                    writer.write_table(_table(batch))
                    batch = []
            writer.write_table(_table(batch))
        tmp.replace(out)
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return out

The GEO lane: family SOFT and filelist.txt of every target Series, from GEO's site.

Each Series' family SOFT is streamed over a few kept-open HTTPS connections with its sample and platform data tables stripped on the way; the stored text starts with the original file's size and sha256. A fetch-failed Series is asked once more before the lane ends, and again on the next run; a soft-missing one is not. Each held Series then gets its filelist.txt, a 404 saved as an empty text. Results are written as parts for the pack step; a saved item makes no request.

def run(
    root: Path,
    series: Iterable[str],
    *,
    client: EntrezClient,
    date: str | None = None,
    connections: int = CONNECTIONS,
) -> LaneReport:
    """Fetch the family SOFT of each Series and its SubSeries, then each held one's filelist.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root; parts go under ``work/parts/``.
    series : iterable of str
        The target Series.
    client : EntrezClient
        The NCBI seam; only its ``stream`` is used.
    date : str or None
        The fetch date to record; defaults to today's UTC date.
    connections : int
        Connections kept open; halved on HTTP 429, 503 or repeated timeouts.

    Returns
    -------
    LaneReport
        Counts over every Series met, saved before this run or now.
    """
    date = date or dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).date().isoformat()
    todo = sorted({s.strip().upper() for s in series})
    seen: set[str] = set()
    retried = False
    with _Pool(client, connections) as pool:
        rounds = 0
        while todo:
            rounds += 1
            seen |= set(todo)
            what = "retry of failed" if retried else f"round {rounds}"
            _fetch_soft(root, pool, todo, date, f"Series SOFT, {what}")
            todo = sorted(_named_subseries(root, set(todo)) - seen)
            if not todo and not retried:
                retried = True
                todo = sorted(_failed(root, seen - _soft_held(root, seen)))
        held = sorted(_soft_held(root, seen))
        _fetch_filelists(root, pool, held, date)
        if len(_accessions(root, raw.GEO_FILELIST, set(held))) < len(held):
            _fetch_filelists(root, pool, held, date)
    reasons = Counter(text.split("\n", 1)[0] for text in _gap_texts(root, seen - set(held)))
    return LaneReport(
        held=len(held),
        soft_missing=reasons[gaps.SOFT_MISSING],
        fetch_failed=reasons[gaps.FETCH_FAILED],
        filelists=len(_accessions(root, raw.GEO_FILELIST, set(held))),
    )

Return family SOFT without its sample and platform data tables, size and sha256 first.

Each table goes with its begin and end lines; every other line is kept as served.

Source code in src/labdata/store/geo_lane.py 
def strip_soft(chunks: Iterable[bytes]) -> str:
    """Return family SOFT without its sample and platform data tables, size and sha256 first.

    Each table goes with its begin and end lines; every other line is kept as served.
    """
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    size = 0
    kept: list[bytes] = []
    inside = False
    carry = b""
    for chunk in itertools.chain(chunks, [None]):
        if chunk is None:
            block, carry = carry, b""
        else:
            digest.update(chunk)
            size += len(chunk)
            cut = chunk.rfind(b"\n") + 1
            if not cut:
                carry += chunk
                continue
            block, carry = carry + chunk[:cut], chunk[cut:]
        at = 0
        while at < len(block):
            match = (_TABLE_END if inside else _TABLE_BEGIN).search(block, at)
            if not inside:
                kept.append(block[at : match.start() if match else len(block)])
            if not match:
                break
            at = match.end() if inside else match.start()
            inside = not inside
    body = b"".join(kept).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    return f"{SIZE_LINE}{size}\n{SHA256_LINE}{digest.hexdigest()}\n{body}"

The E-utilities lane: the SRA EXPERIMENT_PACKAGE of every GEO-linked experiment.

The experiment list is the union of the SRX accessions in saved SOFT !Sample_relation lines and the SRA_Accessions.tab experiments with Center=GEO and a GSM alias, each with its tab status. Packages come from efetch in batches, several calls in flight under the client's shared rate cap. Each bucket's piece is split into parts of a few thousand experiments, so a preempted run loses at most a few open parts. An experiment NCBI serves no package for is saved as an sra-xml row with empty text, which the build lists in its notes. Each run also asks again for a saved package that is empty while the tab says live, or that the current build notes as not well-formed. Every step streams: the tab, the SOFT text and the list are read in chunks and spilled to Parquet under work/eutils/.

        If the store has no such snapshot.
    """
    snap = snapshots.snapshot(root, snapshots.SRA_ACCESSIONS, date)
    folder = root / "work" / "eutils"
    tab = _tab_experiments(snap, folder / f"tab-{snap.date}.parquet")
    wanted = None if series is None else set(series)
    soft = _soft_experiments(root, folder / "soft.parquet", wanted)
    geo = "geo"
    if wanted is not None:
        samples = _samples(root, folder / "samples.parquet", wanted)
        geo = f"geo AND gsm IN (SELECT accession FROM read_parquet('{samples}'))"
    out = list_path(root, snap.date)
    tmp = temp_beside(out)
    try:
        with extract.connect(root) as con:
            con.execute(
                f"""
                COPY (
                  WITH tab AS (
                    SELECT accession, any_value(status) AS status, bool_or({geo}) AS geo
                    FROM read_parquet('{tab}') GROUP BY accession
                  ),
                  wanted AS (
                    SELECT accession FROM tab WHERE geo
                    UNION SELECT accession FROM read_parquet('{soft}')
                  )
                  SELECT w.accession, coalesce(t.status, '') AS status
                  FROM wanted w LEFT JOIN tab t USING (accession)
                  WHERE regexp_matches(w.accession, '^[A-Z]+[0-9]+$')
                  ORDER BY regexp_extract(w.accession, '^[A-Z]+'), length(w.accession),
                           w.accession
                ) TO '{tmp}' (FORMAT parquet)
                """
            )
        tmp.replace(out)
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return out

def fetch_packages(
    root: Path,
    experiments: Path,
    *,
    client: EntrezClient,
    date: str,
    batch: int = BATCH,
    inflight: int = INFLIGHT,
    part_size: int = EXPERIMENTS_PER_PART,
    log_every: float = EVERY,
) -> LaneReport:
    """Fetch the package of every listed experiment no part or raw bucket holds yet.

    Calls finish in any order: a slow call holds back only its own part, while at most
    :data:`OPEN_PARTS` parts are open at once.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    experiments : pathlib.Path
        The list from :func:`experiment_list`.
    client : EntrezClient
        The Entrez seam; its limiter sets the rate.
    date : str
        The fetch date recorded on every row.
    batch, inflight, part_size : int
        Experiments per call, calls in flight, experiments per part.
    log_every : float
        Seconds between progress lines.

    Returns
    -------
    LaneReport
        Counts for this run. An experiment whose call failed is asked once more before the
        lane ends; if that fails too it is not saved, so the next run asks for it again. A new
        one NCBI has no package for is saved with an empty text and counted in ``missing``.
        Saved bad packages are asked again: ``reasked`` counts them, ``recovered`` those that
        came back good and replace the saved copy.
    """
    sizes = (batch, inflight, part_size)
    noted = gaps.noted(root, gaps.UNPARSABLE_PACKAGE)
    first, settled = _fetch_once(root, experiments, client, date, sizes, log_every, noted, set())
    report = first
    if first.failed:
        logger.info("asking again for the %d experiments whose calls failed", first.failed)
        last, _ = _fetch_once(root, experiments, client, date, sizes, log_every, noted, settled)
        report = LaneReport(
            first.fetched + last.fetched,
            first.missing + last.missing,
            last.failed,
            len(settled) + last.reasked,
            first.recovered + last.recovered,
        )
    logger.info(
        "asked again for %d saved bad packages; %d came back good",
        report.reasked,
        report.recovered,
    )
    return report

def bucket_of(source: str, accession: str) -> str:
    """Return the bucket an accession's rows go in within one source.

    The bucket keeps the accession's prefix and its number with the last digits of the
    source's width written ``n``: at width 10,000, ``GSE246310`` -> ``GSE24nnnn``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the accession is not letters then digits.
    KeyError
        If the source has no width in :data:`WIDTHS`.
    """
    digits = len(str(WIDTHS[source])) - 1
    if match := _ACCESSION.match(accession):
        return f"{match[1]}{match[2][:-digits]}{'n' * digits}"
    raise ValueError(f"no raw bucket for {accession!r}")

def pieces(root: Path, source: str, accessions: Iterable[str]) -> list[Piece]:
    """Split accessions into pieces, one per bucket, leaving out every saved accession.

    An accession is saved when a raw bucket row or a part holds it, or a part's piece asked
    for it and got no row. A bucket with nothing left to fetch yields no piece.
    """
    by_bucket: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    for accession in accessions:
        by_bucket[bucket_of(source, accession)].add(accession)
    done = _done(root, source, set(by_bucket))
    return [
        Piece(source, bucket, tuple(sorted(wanted - done[bucket])))
        for bucket, wanted in sorted(by_bucket.items())
        if wanted - done[bucket]
    ]

def write_part(
    root: Path,
    piece: Piece,
    rows: Iterable[RawRow],
    *,
    record_asked: bool = True,
    chunk_bytes: int = SORT_CHUNK_BYTES,
) -> Path:
    """Write one piece's rows as a part file, chunk by chunk, renamed into place when whole.

    Each chunk is sorted by accession and written as one row group, so memory holds one
    chunk. With ``record_asked``, the part records ``piece.todo`` as asked, so an accession
    with no row is not fetched again before the next pack.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a row belongs to another bucket.
    """
    folder = parts_dir(root, piece.source)
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tag = hashlib.sha256("\n".join(piece.todo).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    path = folder / f"{piece.bucket}.{tag}.parquet"

    def checked() -> Iterator[RawRow]:
        for row in rows:
            if bucket_of(piece.source, row.accession) != piece.bucket:
                raise ValueError(f"{row.accession} is not in bucket {piece.bucket}")
            yield row

    listed = "\n".join(piece.todo) if record_asked else ""
    schema = SCHEMA.with_metadata({ASKED_KEY: listed.encode()})
    write_sorted_runs(path, checked(), schema, chunk_bytes=chunk_bytes)
    return path

def write_sorted_runs(
    path: Path, rows: Iterable[RawRow], schema: pa.Schema, *, chunk_bytes: int = SORT_CHUNK_BYTES
) -> None:
    """Write rows to ``path`` one chunk at a time, each chunk sorted by accession.

    A chunk is written as :data:`GROUPS_PER_CHUNK` row groups, so a reader merging many
    sorted runs holds one small row group of each. The file appears by a rename once whole.
    Rows already in order make a sorted file.
    """
    tmp = writer_temp(path)
    try:
        with pq.ParquetWriter(tmp, schema) as writer:
            chunk: list[RawRow] = []
            size = 0
            for row in rows:
                chunk.append(row)
                size += len(row.raw_text)
                if size >= chunk_bytes or len(chunk) >= SORT_CHUNK_ROWS:
                    _write_chunk(writer, chunk, schema, chunk_bytes)
                    chunk, size = [], 0
            if chunk:
                _write_chunk(writer, chunk, schema, chunk_bytes)
        tmp.replace(path)
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)

def saved(root: Path, source: str, accessions: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return the saved raw text of those ``accessions`` that have a row, in raw or a part.

    A part's row wins over a raw bucket's, and a newer part's over an older one's.
    """
    wanted = set(accessions)
    buckets = {bucket_of(source, a) for a in wanted}
    paths = [root / "raw" / source / f"{bucket}.parquet" for bucket in sorted(buckets)]
    paths += [p for p in part_files(root, source) if part_bucket(p) in buckets]
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for path in paths:
        out |= {row.accession: row.raw_text for row in _read(path) if row.accession in wanted}
    return out

    """
    out = build_dir / "gaps.parquet"
    kv = f"{DATE_KEY}: {extract.sql_string(date)}"
    if fraction is not None:
        kv += f", {FRACTION_KEY}: {extract.sql_string(repr(fraction))}"
    reasons = ", ".join(extract.sql_string(r) for r in REASONS[:-1])
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        con.execute(
            f"""COPY (
            WITH g AS ({_gap_rows(root)})
            SELECT t.accession,
              CASE WHEN g.reason IN ({reasons}) THEN g.reason ELSE '{UNEXPLAINED}' END
                AS reason,
              CASE WHEN g.reason IS NULL OR g.reason IN ({reasons}) THEN g.detail
                ELSE 'recorded reason: ' || g.reason END AS detail
            FROM (SELECT DISTINCT accession FROM {_read(target_list)}) t
            LEFT JOIN g USING (accession)
            WHERE t.accession NOT IN ({_held_series(build_dir)})
            ORDER BY CAST(substr(t.accession, 4) AS BIGINT)
            ) TO {extract.sql_string(str(out))}
            (FORMAT parquet, KV_METADATA {{{kv}}})"""
        )
        counts = dict(
            con.execute(f"SELECT reason, count(*) FROM {_read(out)} GROUP BY 1").fetchall()
        )
        target = _count(con, f"SELECT count(DISTINCT accession) FROM {_read(target_list)}")
    by_reason = {reason: int(counts.get(reason, 0)) for reason in REASONS}
    summary: dict[str, object] = {"snapshot_date": date}
    if fraction is not None:
        summary["fraction"] = fraction
    return summary | {
        "target": target,
        "held": target - sum(by_reason.values()),
        "gaps": by_reason,
    }

def write_notes(
    root: Path,
    build_dir: Path,
    target_list: Path,
    extra: Iterable[Note] = (),
    experiments: Path | None = None,
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Write ``notes.parquet``: type disagreements, failed package fetches, then ``extra``.

    A failed package fetch is an experiment on the E-utilities lane's list ``experiments``
    that ``raw/sra-xml/`` does not hold.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to int
        The note count by kind.
    """
    out = build_dir / "notes.parquet"
    series = build_dir / "records" / "geo-series.parquet"
    rows = list(extra)
    extra_table = pa.table(
        {
            "accession": [n.accession for n in rows],
            "kind": [n.kind for n in rows],
            "detail": [n.detail for n in rows],
        },
        schema=NOTE_SCHEMA,
    )
    disagree = (
        f"""SELECT t.accession, '{TYPE_DISAGREES}' AS kind,
              'snapshot: ' || t.gdstype || ' | SOFT: ' || coalesce(s.types, 'no type') AS detail
            FROM {_read(target_list)} t
            JOIN (SELECT accession FROM {_read(series)}) r USING (accession)
            LEFT JOIN (
              SELECT accession, string_agg(DISTINCT f.value, '; ' ORDER BY f.value) AS types,
                bool_or(contains(lower(f.value), {extract.sql_string(targets.SEQUENCING)}))
                  AS sequencing
              FROM (SELECT accession, unnest(fields) AS f FROM {_read(series)})
              WHERE f.name = 'Series_type' GROUP BY accession
            ) s USING (accession)
            WHERE NOT coalesce(s.sequencing, false)"""
        if series.is_file()
        else "SELECT * FROM extra WHERE false"
    )
    unfetched = "SELECT * FROM extra WHERE false"
    saved = root / "raw" / raw.SRA_XML
    if experiments is not None and experiments.is_file():
        held = (
            f"SELECT accession FROM {_read(saved / '*.parquet')}"
            if any(saved.glob("*.parquet"))
            else "SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS accession WHERE false"
        )
        unfetched = (
            f"SELECT accession, '{PACKAGE_FETCH_FAILED}' AS kind, "
            f"'no package saved; a rerun asks again' AS detail FROM {_read(experiments)} "
            f"WHERE accession NOT IN ({held})"
        )
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        con.register("extra", extra_table)
        con.execute(
            f"COPY (SELECT * FROM ({disagree} UNION ALL {unfetched} UNION ALL "
            "SELECT * FROM extra) "
            f"ORDER BY kind, accession, detail) TO {extract.sql_string(str(out))} (FORMAT parquet)"
        )
        counts = con.execute(f"SELECT kind, count(*) FROM {_read(out)} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1")
        return {str(kind): int(n) for kind, n in counts.fetchall()}

def coverage(root: Path, build_dir: Path) -> Coverage:
    """Check one build against the target list of the snapshot its gaps were made from.

    The target list is re-read from the snapshot, so a stale or partial ``gaps.parquet``
    fails rather than agreeing with itself. A round's build is checked against its sample.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If the build has no ``gaps.parquet`` or its snapshot is gone.
    """
    gaps_file = build_dir / "gaps.parquet"
    if not gaps_file.is_file():
        raise StoreBuildError(
            f"{build_dir} has no gaps.parquet; rebuild with `labdata store build`"
        )
    meta = pq.read_metadata(gaps_file).metadata or {}
    date = meta[DATE_KEY.encode()].decode()
    fraction = meta.get(FRACTION_KEY.encode())
    target_list = targets.target_list(root, date, None if fraction is None else float(fraction))
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW t AS SELECT DISTINCT accession FROM {_read(target_list)}")
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW h AS {_held_series(build_dir)}")
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW g AS SELECT accession, reason, detail FROM {_read(gaps_file)}")
        target = _count(con, "SELECT count(*) FROM t")
        held = _count(con, "SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE accession IN (SELECT accession FROM h)")
        by_reason = dict(con.execute("SELECT reason, count(*) FROM g GROUP BY 1").fetchall())
        problems = f"""
            SELECT accession, 'not held and no gap row' FROM t
              WHERE accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM h)
              AND accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM g)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, 'gap row for a held Series' FROM g
              WHERE accession IN (SELECT accession FROM h)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, 'gap row for a Series not on the target list' FROM g
              WHERE accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM t)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, '{UNEXPLAINED}' || coalesce(': ' || detail, '') FROM g
              WHERE reason = '{UNEXPLAINED}'"""
        failures = _count(con, f"SELECT count(*) FROM ({problems})")
        failing = con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM ({problems}) ORDER BY 1, 2 LIMIT {NAMED}").fetchall()
        notes = build_dir / "notes.parquet"
        failed_experiments = (
            _count(
                con,
                f"SELECT count(*) FROM {_read(notes)} WHERE kind = '{PACKAGE_FETCH_FAILED}'",
            )
            if notes.is_file()
            else 0
        )
    return Coverage(
        snapshot_date=date,
        target=target,
        held=held,
        gaps={reason: int(by_reason.get(reason, 0)) for reason in (*REASONS, *by_reason)},
        failing=tuple((str(a), str(p)) for a, p in failing),
        failures=failures,
        failed_experiments=failed_experiments,
    )

items.title: prune
items.text:
Delete the builds and snapshots the store no longer reads, after a grace period.

A non-current build goes once the store switched away from it more than the grace period ago, GRACE by default. A snapshot goes once it is older than the one the current build reads and every build that read it went out of use more than the grace period ago; its extract parts under work/ go with it. A snapshot newer than the current build's is waiting for the next build and stays. Neither the current build nor what it reads is ever deleted.

def prune(
    root: Path, *, now: dt.datetime | None = None, grace: dt.timedelta = GRACE
) -> PruneReport:
    """Delete old builds and unread snapshots, keeping everything inside the grace period.

    A build switched away from before switch times were recorded counts as switched away
    when the current build was switched to. After deleting anything, it rewrites the root
    ``README.md`` so its sizes stay current.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    now : datetime.datetime or None
        The time to measure the grace period from; defaults to the current UTC time.
    grace : datetime.timedelta
        How long a build stays after the store switched away from it: ``GRACE``, 24 hours,
        by default. Zero deletes at once.

    Returns
    -------
    PruneReport
        The folders deleted.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If a build, prune or copy of this store is running.
    """
    now = now or dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC)
    with build_lock(root):
        marker = root / MARKER
        settings = read_marker(root)
        current = settings.get(BUILD_KEY)
        if not current:
            return PruneReport()
        switched = _time(settings.get(SWITCHED_KEY)) or dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(
            marker.stat().st_mtime, dt.UTC
        )
        away: dict[str, str] = settings.get(SWITCHED_AWAY_KEY, {})
        builds = sorted(
            p for p in (root / "builds").glob("*") if p.is_dir() and not p.name.startswith(".")
        )
        reads = {b.name: _reads(b) for b in builds}
        unused_since = {
            b.name: _time(away.get(b.name)) or switched for b in builds if b.name != current
        }
        old = [root / "builds" / name for name, t in unused_since.items() if now - t > grace]
        latest = dict(reads.get(str(current), set()))
        snaps = []
        for folder in sorted((root / "snapshots").glob("*/*")):
            source, date = folder.parent.name, folder.name
            if not (folder.is_dir() and _DATE.match(date)) or date >= latest.get(source, date):
                continue
            readers = [n for n, t in unused_since.items() if (source, date) in reads[n]]
            if now - max((unused_since[n] for n in readers), default=switched) > grace:
                snaps.append(folder)
        for folder in [*old, *snaps]:
            shutil.rmtree(folder)
        for folder in snaps:
            shutil.rmtree(
                extract.extract_dir(root, folder.parent.name, folder.name), ignore_errors=True
            )
        if any(p.name in away for p in old):
            settings[SWITCHED_AWAY_KEY] = {k: v for k, v in away.items() if not _gone(root, k)}
            write_marker(root, settings)
        if old or snaps:
            readme.try_write(root)
        return PruneReport([*old, *snaps])

def write(root: Path) -> Path:
    """Write ``<root>/README.md`` for the build the marker names.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The README written.

    Raises
    ------
    NotAStoreError
        If the root has no marker, or the marker names no build.
    """
    settings = read_marker(root)
    build = settings.get("build")
    if not build:
        raise NotAStoreError(f"{root / MARKER} names no build; run `labdata store build`")
    folder = root / "builds" / str(build)
    manifest_path = folder / MANIFEST
    manifest = (
        json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if manifest_path.is_file() else {}
    )
    made = manifest.get("produced_by")
    snaps = manifest.get("inputs", {}).get("snapshots", {})
    sizes = [(f"builds/{build}/", _size(folder))] + [
        (f"{name}/", _size(root / name)) for name in _SIZED if (root / name).is_dir()
    ]
    text = string.Template(_template()).substitute(
        build=build,
        switched=settings.get("switched", "an unrecorded time"),
        made_by=_made_by(made),
        snapshot_table=_table(
            ("Source", "Date", "File"),
            [(f"`{s}`", v["date"], f"`{v['name']}`") for s, v in sorted(snaps.items())],
        ),
        size_table=_table(("Folder", "Size"), [(f"`{n}`", _human(b)) for n, b in sizes]),
    )
    out = root / README
    write_atomic(out, text)
    return out

The copy holds the marker, the root README.md, the snapshots the current build read, raw/ and the current build; work/, support/ and older builds are left out, and the bucket's copies of them are deleted. def copy(root: Path, destination: str | None = None) -> CopyResult:
    """Copy the store's current state to ``destination`` with rclone.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    destination : str or None
        An rclone path, ``<remote>:<bucket>/<path>``; defaults to the marker's ``copy_to``.

    Returns
    -------
    CopyResult
        ``skipped`` is true, with a message, when rclone's Google login has expired.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreCopyError
        If the store does not open, its current build is incomplete, no destination is set,
        or rclone fails for another reason. rclone is not called when the store is refused.
    StoreBuildError
        If a build, prune or copy of this store is running.
    """
    try:
        store = open_store(root)
    except NotAStoreError as err:
        raise StoreCopyError(f"copy refused: {err}") from None
    dest = destination or store.settings.get(COPY_TO_KEY)
    if not dest:
        raise StoreCopyError(
            f"no destination: pass --to <remote>:<bucket>/<path> or set "
            f"{COPY_TO_KEY} in {root / MARKER}"
        )
    with build_lock(root):
        selected = _selected(root, store.settings.get("build"))
        src = str(root)
        for args in (
            ["rclone", "copy", src, dest, *selected, "--filter=- **", *_PROGRESS],
            [
                "rclone",
                "sync",
                src,
                dest,
                "--delete-excluded",
                *selected,
                f"--filter=+ /{MARKER}",
                "--filter=- **",
                *_PROGRESS,
            ],
        ):
            done = _run_rclone(args)
            if done.returncode == 0:
                continue
            if _EXPIRED.search(done.stderr):
                remote = dest.split(":", 1)[0]
                return CopyResult(
                    str(dest),
                    skipped=True,
                    message=(
                        f"rclone's Google login has expired, so the bucket is behind the store. "
                        f"Run `rclone config reconnect {remote}:`, then `labdata store copy`."
                    ),
                )
            raise StoreCopyError(f"rclone {args[1]} failed ({done.returncode}): {done.stderr}")
    return CopyResult(str(dest))

items.title: Copy the store to GCS
items.text: The store keeps one current state on the cluster and a full copy in a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket. Any full copy is the store, so work can go on from the bucket if the cluster copy is lost. The tool that moves files is rclone, which comes with the pixi environment.

items.title: Set up once
items.text:
Make an rclone remote of type Google Cloud Storage, here called gcs:

pixi run rclone config

Then name the place in the bucket in the store's labdata-store.toml:

copy_to = "gcs:<bucket>/<store>"

items.title: Log in each day
items.text:
Your Google login for rclone lasts one day. Renew it before a copy:

pixi run rclone config reconnect gcs:

A cluster node has no web browser. Answer n when rclone asks to use one. It then prints an rclone authorize ... command. Run that command on a computer with a browser, log in, and paste the token it prints back into the prompt on the node.

items.title: Prune and copy
items.text:
labdata store prune
labdata store copy

prune deletes builds and snapshots the current build no longer reads. It keeps each one for a grace period after it goes out of use, so a reader can finish; the API reference gives its length. --grace 0 deletes them at once: use it only as a one-off to tidy a store nobody is reading.

copy sends the marker file, the store's README.md, the current snapshots, raw/ and the current build, and deletes anything else in the bucket's copy. It leaves out work/ and support/. It will not run unless the current build is complete. When the login has expired, it stops and exits cleanly:

rclone's Google login has expired, so the bucket is behind the store. Run `rclone config reconnect gcs:`, then `labdata store copy`.

Log in, then run labdata store copy again. Files already sent are skipped.

items.title: Read the store on another computer
items.text:
Copy the store down, check it against the bucket, and point labdata at it:

rclone copy gcs:<bucket>/<store> /data/store
rclone check gcs:<bucket>/<store> /data/store
export LABDATA_STORE=/data/store

To only read the store, copy just the marker and the build it names:

rclone copy gcs:<bucket>/<store> /data/store \
  --include "/labdata-store.toml" --include "/builds/<build>/**"

items.title: Run the full download
items.text: One command fetches every target GEO Series and the records it links to, builds the tables, switches the store to the new build, deletes old builds and copies the store to the bucket. It runs on the cluster as one Slurm job, and you can stop and restart it at any time.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• Download the bulk snapshots with scripts/bulk/download_ncbi_bulk.py. The run uses the newest snapshot of each source.
  • Save your NCBI email and API key with labdata ncbi configure.
  • To copy the store at the end, set copy_to in labdata-store.toml and log in to rclone that day. See Copy the store to GCS. Without copy_to, the run skips the copy and says so.

items.title: Start a round
items.text:
Run the download in three rounds: 1%, then 10%, then all of the target list. Each round's Series are a fixed random sample, and a smaller round's Series are all inside the next one. A larger round never fetches again what a smaller round saved.

From the repository folder on the cluster:

export LABDATA_STORE=/path/to/store
sbatch scripts/store/run.sbatch 0.01   # round 1
sbatch scripts/store/run.sbatch 0.1    # round 2
sbatch scripts/store/run.sbatch        # round 3: every target Series

Start the next round only when the last one looks right. Off a cluster, or for a quick try, run the same steps straight away:

labdata store run --fraction 0.01

items.title: Watch it
items.text:
The job log, labdata-run.<job id>.log, shows each step as it starts and ends. The fetch steps print a line at least once a minute:

2026-10-15 21:04:10 labdata.store.geo_lane 1,204/1,985 Series SOFT, round 1 (60.7%), 26.8/s, errors: timeout 3, finish ~2026-10-15 21:05 UTC

Each step also writes its own log under work/run/<snapshot date>-<fraction>/logs/ in the store. That folder holds the round's markers too: one file per finished step.

At the end, the coverage step checks that every Series in the round is held or explained:

Target Series: 1985 (geo-series snapshot 2026-10-14)
Held: 1983
Gaps: 2
  soft-missing: 2
  fetch-failed: 0
  unexplained: 0
SRA experiments fetch-failed: 0 (not Series gaps)
Coverage passes.

If coverage fails, the run stops there: it does not delete old builds or copy the store.

items.title: Resume
items.text:
Submit the same command again. The run starts at the first step that did not finish, and the fetch steps skip every Series and experiment already saved. A job that the cluster stops to make room is put back in the queue and resumes by itself.

The fetch steps ask once more for every item that failed before they finish. A Series that still fails is a fetch-failed gap, and an SRA experiment that still fails is counted on the SRA experiments fetch-failed line. To ask for those again, submit the same round again: the fetch steps ask only for what failed, and the steps after them run again. Nothing saved is fetched twice.

items.title: After the last round
items.text:
To keep each round's logs with the store, copy them into support/. <round> is the round's folder under work/run/, such as 2026-10-14-all:

scripts/store/keep_run_logs.sh "$LABDATA_STORE" <round>

The build writes README.md at the store root. It says what each folder holds, how it was made, and how to open the store as a database. After you copy logs into support/ or delete work/, write it again with fresh folder sizes:

labdata store readme

The run keeps the old build for a grace period after the switch, so a reader that opened it can finish; the API reference gives its length. labdata store prune --grace 0 deletes it and the snapshots only it read at once. Use that only as a one-off to tidy a store nobody is reading, not as a refresh step. Prune never deletes the current build or anything it reads.

items.title: Go deeper
items.text: The steps are also commands of their own: labdata store pack, build, coverage, prune and copy. Run labdata store --help to list them, and see the API reference for the modules behind them.

items.title: GEO Series: from study to FASTQ
items.text: This tutorial goes from a GEO accession to downloaded FASTQ in a few short steps, using a real study — GSE47966 (Global epigenomic reconfiguration during mammalian brain development). First, make sure you've installed the package and set your NCBI email.
path: GEO Series: from study to FASTQ

items.title: 1. Look up a GEO Series
items.text:
Start from any GEO accession (GSE…). Building the handle is instant; reading a field is what triggers the lookup.

from labdata import Series

gse = Series("GSE47966")     # just a handle — no network yet

gse.title         # 'Global epigenomic reconfiguration during mammalian brain development'
gse.organism      # 'Homo sapiens; Mus musculus'
gse.platforms     # [Platform('GPL13112'), Platform('GPL11154')]
gse.samples       # [Sample('GSM1173819'), Sample('GSM1173773'), ...]   (65 samples)
gse.experiments   # [Experiment('SRX314994'), Experiment('SRX314993'), ...]   (65 experiments)
gse.url           # 'https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE47966'

Each linked item (a sample, an experiment, a run) is its own object you can drill into the same way. See the API reference for everything they expose.
path: GEO Series: from study to FASTQ

items.title: 2. Get the SRA run table
items.text:
Want the table you'd normally click through on NCBI's SRA Run Selector — one row per sequencing run, with library and instrument details? Ask for it directly. It comes back as a pandas DataFrame, so you can filter, sort, and export it however you like.

table = gse.make_sra_run_table()      # one row per run (392 in this study)

table[["Run", "Instrument", "ReadStructure", "Bases", "LibraryLayout"]].head(3)

         Run           Instrument ReadStructure        Bases LibraryLayout
0  SRR907554  Illumina HiSeq 2000            50  10100000000        SINGLE
1  SRR907555  Illumina HiSeq 2000            50  10100000000        SINGLE
2  SRR907556  Illumina HiSeq 2000            50  10100000000        SINGLE
...

ReadStructure gives the length of each read in a spot, joined with +: a single-end 50 bp run reads 50, while a paired run with a 28 bp barcode and a 94 bp cDNA read reads 28+94 — a quick way to spot single-cell chemistries.

table.to_csv("GSE47966_runs.csv", index=False)   # hand it off to collaborators
path: GEO Series: from study to FASTQ

items.title: 3. Download all FASTQ files
items.text:
One call fetches the FASTQ for every run in the study, running a Snakemake pipeline (prefetch → extract → compress) over sra-tools under the hood. Files are organized by study → experiment → run and gzipped for you:

gse.download("./fastq", ncbi_parallel=3, cores=16)   # ≤3 downloads at once, 16 cores total

The two knobs are independent, which is the point: ncbi_parallel caps how many runs prefetch from NCBI at once (keep it low to stay friendly with NCBI), while cores bounds total CPU for the local extraction/gzip work. So downloads keep the network busy while cores chew through already-fetched runs, instead of the two blocking each other. On an HPC allocation, set cores to your allotted cores.

{'SRR921999': True, 'SRR922000': True, 'SRR922001': True, ...}     # each run: success?

The files land in a tidy tree:

fastq/
└── GSE47966/
    ├── SRX314994/
    │   ├── SRR921999.fastq.gz
    │   ├── SRR922000.fastq.gz
    │   └── ...
    └── SRX314993/
        └── ...

Good to know

  • This downloads real sequencing data, which can be large — point output_dir somewhere with room to spare. If free space looks tight, the download prints a rough warning before it starts (it never blocks).
  • GSE47966's runs are single-end, so each gives one .fastq.gz; paired-end runs produce _1/_2 files instead.
  • Interruptible. A finished run leaves a .<run>.done marker, so re-running download() skips what's already done — an interrupted download resumes without re-fetching SRA data (and prefetch itself resumes a partial .sra). Safe after a Ctrl-C or an HPC walltime kill.
  • Modest peak disk. Snakemake reclaims each intermediate the moment the next step consumes it — a run's .sra the moment its FASTQ is extracted, the uncompressed FASTQ the moment they're gzipped — and drains extraction/compression before fetching more, so only a handful of .sra sit on disk at once. Lower ncbi_parallel to shrink that working set further.
  • Pass keep_sra=True to keep each run's .sra next to its FASTQ instead of reclaiming it after extraction (useful for re-extracting later), or prefetch_only=True to just stage the .sra files without extracting.
  • Needs sra-tools and pigz on your system (see Installation); Snakemake comes with liulab-data.

Just one experiment?

Series.download does the whole study. To grab a single experiment instead, use SraDownloader — see the API reference. Pass original=True for that experiment's original-format files.

Have a BioProject instead?

BioProject exposes the same download() — BioProject("PRJNA1027859").download("./fastq") lays the FASTQ out identically, under a PRJNA…/ directory. The labdata geo download command auto-detects which you gave it, so GSE… and PRJ… accessions both just work.
path: GEO Series: from study to FASTQ

items.title: When the .sra is missing or useless
items.text:
Sometimes a run's SRA-normalized .sra is gone or wrong. For example, a 10X run's .sra may keep only one read of a pair. The submitter's original-format files (listed under "Data access" in the SRA Run Browser) are still there. Name those experiments with original_srx to fetch them as-is. This downloads only; it does not extract:

gse.download("./fastq", original_srx=["SRX34567890"])

labdata geo download GSE310667 --original-srx SRX34567890

The files land under …/<SRX>/<SRR>/ with their original names and are md5-checked against NCBI. Everything else in the study still takes the normal sra-tools path. This only sets the mode. To also narrow which experiments run, add --select-srx/select_srx (repeatable, or a whitelist file). Original format varies from study to study, so labdata downloads it and leaves the processing to you. It needs curl in addition to sra-tools/pigz. When the original file is a 10x cellranger BAM, the 10x BAM → FASTQ tutorial turns it back into remap-ready FASTQ.
path: GEO Series: from study to FASTQ

items.title: 4. Grab the supplementary files
items.text:
Raw FASTQ isn't the whole story. Authors usually attach supplementary files — processed matrices, peak calls, bigWigs, READMEs — to the Series. List them and grab their download URLs directly:

gse.supplementary_files       # ['GSE47966_RAW.tar', 'GSE47966_README.txt', 'filelist.txt']
gse.supplementary_file_urls   # full https URLs you can download
gse.supplementary_http_url    # the suppl/ directory itself

These are often where the useful, ready-to-analyze outputs live — see what's not in GEO for why they matter.
path: GEO Series: from study to FASTQ

items.title: Recovering FASTQ from a 10x cellranger BAM
items.text:
Some 10x Genomics studies upload a cellranger BAM as their raw data, and SRA's normalized .sra for those runs is unusable — often it kept only one read of the pair, so fasterq-dump can't reconstruct the barcodes. The fix is to go back to the submitter's original BAM and turn that into FASTQ with 10x's own bamtofastq, which reads the 10x tags to split the barcode (R1), cDNA (R2), and index (I1) reads correctly — ready to remap with STARsolo.

This is a two-step flow: download the original BAMs, then convert them.
path: Recovering FASTQ from a 10x cellranger BAM

items.title: 1. Download the original-format BAMs
items.text:
Fetch the submitter's files for the affected experiments (see the GEO Series tutorial's note on original files):

labdata geo download GSE208154 --original-srx SRX16000000 -o ./data

They land under ./data/GSE208154/<SRX>/<SRR>/<name>.bam.
path: Recovering FASTQ from a 10x cellranger BAM

items.title: 2. Convert the BAMs to FASTQ
items.text:
labdata tenx bamtofastq GSE208154 -o ./data --cores 16

labdata tenx bamtofastq auto-detects which runs carry a 10x BAM (from the SRA Data Locator listing) and converts each one that's on disk, driving bamtofastq as a Snakemake DAG. The result is laid out like the download pipeline — flat under the experiment directory, one prefix per run — so a later STARsolo step parses one layout:

data/GSE208154/<SRX>/
  <SRR>_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz   # barcode + UMI
  <SRR>_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz   # cDNA
  <SRR>_S1_L001_I1_001.fastq.gz   # sample index
  …

The R1/R2/I1 and lane markers are preserved (STARsolo needs them), while the files sit flat beside the experiment's other runs and glob as <SRX>/<SRR>*.fastq.gz, just like a normal download.

Good to know

  • Conversion-only. This step reads BAMs that are already on disk; run the original-format download first. Pointing both commands at the same -o directory is intended — they share the <GSE>/<SRX>/<SRR>/ layout.
  • Interruptible. A finished run leaves a .<run>.tenx.done marker, so re-running skips what's already converted. Safe after a Ctrl-C or HPC walltime kill.
  • --cores bounds total CPU across runs; --threads-per-run sets each bamtofastq's --nthreads. On an HPC allocation, pass --cores $SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE.
  • Auto-detection uses one SDL lookup per run. Pass --all-runs to skip it and convert every run of the selected experiments (e.g. when you already know they're all 10x), or --select-srx to narrow which experiments are considered.
  • On an offline HPC compute node, pass --from-disk: the run list is built by scanning the downloaded <SRX>/<SRR>/*.bam tree instead of querying NCBI, so no network or credentials are needed.
  • Pass --remove-bam to delete each run's source BAM once its FASTQ are produced — it reclaims the large original, and only fires after a run converts successfully (an interrupted run keeps its BAM for the resumed rerun).
  • Needs 10x_bamtofastq on your system (see Installation); Snakemake comes with liulab-data.

From Python, TenxConverter is the equivalent entry point:

from labdata import TenxConverter

TenxConverter("GSE208154", "./data").convert(cores=16)

See the API reference for the full signature.

items.title: Understanding GEO & SRA
items.text: New to NCBI's sequencing databases? This page gives you just enough of the mental model to use labdata confidently. For the hands-on walkthrough, see the GEO Series tutorial.

items.title: Two databases, one study
items.text:
A sequencing study usually lives in two linked NCBI databases:

  • GEO — the processed, expression-focused side (count matrices, the study's description, sample list).
  • SRA — the raw reads side (the actual FASTQ files you download).

GEO records point into SRA, so you can start from a GEO accession and follow the links all the way down to raw data.

items.title: The hierarchy: study → sample → experiment → run
items.text:
Everything is organized as a tree, from a big project down to individual FASTQ files. Each level has its own ID prefix — and its own class in labdata:

Level Example ID What it is labdata class BioProject PRJNA208503 the whole study / "the paper" BioProject GEO Series GSE47966 the study, as seen in GEO Series GEO Platform GPL13112 the sequencer used Platform GEO Sample GSM1173819 one biological sample Sample SRA Experiment SRX314994 one library + sequencing design Experiment SRA Run SRR921999 the raw FASTQ files Run

(IDs above are from the example study GSE47966.)

A few things worth remembering:

  • It's one-to-many at every level: one project has many samples, each sample can have several experiments, and each experiment can have several runs.
  • SRR (the run) is what you actually download — FASTQ files live at the run level.
  • You'll also see SAMN… (BioSample) — e.g. SAMN02206500 — the SRA-side name for the biological material behind a GSM. labdata reports it as a BioSample field (e.g. a column in the run table) rather than a separate class.

items.title: How labdata reaches this data
items.text:
The package talks to NCBI for you through two channels:

  • Metadata → NCBI Entrez (E-utilities). Every Series, Sample, Experiment, and Run fetches its details from Entrez on demand — building the object costs nothing; the network call happens the first time you read a field, and is cached afterward.
  • Raw FASTQ → sra-tools. download() shells out to prefetch + fasterq-dump to pull and extract the reads for each run.

Because links return real objects, you can walk the tree in plain Python:

from labdata import Series

gse = Series("GSE47966")         # GEO Series (GSE)

for experiment in gse.experiments:   # SRX level
    for run in experiment.runs:      # SRR level — the downloadable units
        print(experiment.accession, run.accession)

That's the whole idea: start at a GEO Series, follow the links down to runs, then download. The GEO Series tutorial shows it end to end.

items.title: What's not in GEO
items.text:
The structured records above (samples, platforms, experiments, runs) are only part of a study. Two things commonly live outside that metadata — don't forget them:

  • Supplementary files. The actual ready-to-analyze outputs — count matrices, peak calls, bigWig tracks, READMEs — are usually attached to the Series as supplementary files, not encoded in the metadata. They're often the most useful part. List and fetch them directly:

    gse.supplementary_files       # ['GSE47966_RAW.tar', 'GSE47966_README.txt', 'filelist.txt']
gse.supplementary_file_urls   # full https URLs you can download

  • Whatever the paper kept elsewhere. GEO doesn't capture everything. Always read the paper's "Data Availability" and "Code Availability" statements: raw or controlled-access data may sit in another repository (dbGaP, EGA, Zenodo, …), and the analysis code typically lives on GitHub — none of which a GEO record will point you to.
